allow_cidrs.description: CIDRs allowed. Empty means everyone not denied.

trusted_proxy_depth.description: Number of trusted proxies in front, so the real client IP is matched.

target_cpu_percent.description: Average CPU utilisation the autoscaler aims for.

cron.description: Cron expression with 5 fields, or @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly, @yearly. At most one run per 5 minutes.

retention_count.description: How many backups to keep. 0 means no limit.

retention_days.description: How many days to keep backups. 0 means no limit.

timezone.description: IANA time zone of the schedule.

context.description: Build context directory, relative to the repository root.

dockerfile.description: Path of the Dockerfile, relative to the repository root.

location.description: Where the build runs: inherit, target (the deploying server) or build_server.

registry.description: Name of the registry that receives images built on a build server.

server.description: Name of the build server when location is build_server.

type.description: Build method: auto, dockerfile, railpack or starter:<node|python|go|ruby|php|static>.

origin_lock.description: Lock the origin so only Cloudflare can reach it.

proxied.description: Route traffic through the Cloudflare proxy (orange cloud). Absent means true for a name NebulaCtrl starts managing, except a wildcard name or a non-HTTP(S) port, which default to DNS only; a name behind a Cloudflare Tunnel is always proxied. Absent never changes a name that already exists: it keeps its current setting. Write false to stay DNS only.

expose_headers.description: Response headers exposed to the browser.

max_age_seconds.description: How long browsers cache the preflight answer.

accept_license.description: Acknowledge the licence of a source-available engine. Required for those engines. Not stored.

flavor.description: Engine flavor, where the engine has more than one.

name.description: Name of the initial database. Defaults to the engine's default.

username.description: Name of the application user. Defaults to the engine's default.

version.description: Engine version. Defaults to the engine's default version.

container_path.description: Where it appears in the container. Defaults to the host path.

host_path.description: Device node on the host, under /dev.

apparmor_unconfined.description: Remove the default AppArmor profile. Unrestricted servers only.

cap_add.description: Linux capabilities to add. NET_ADMIN and SYS_ADMIN need an unrestricted server.

cap_drop.description: Linux capabilities to drop, or ALL.

devices.description: Host devices mapped into the container. Unrestricted servers only.

entrypoint.description: Replaces the image's ENTRYPOINT, as an argv array.

host_sysctls.description: Kernel parameters the application needs on the host, as minimum values. The plan warns when the host is lower.

init.description: Run a minimal init as PID 1.

labels.description: Container labels. com.docker.*, nebulactrl.* and traefik.* are reserved.

pid_host.description: Share the host's PID namespace. Unrestricted servers only.

pids_limit.description: Maximum number of processes and threads.

privileged.description: Give the container host-root equivalent rights. Unrestricted servers only.

runtime.description: OCI runtime configured in the daemon. Unrestricted servers only.

seccomp_unconfined.description: Remove the default syscall filter. Unrestricted servers only.

stop_signal.description: Signal used to stop the container.

sysctls.description: Namespaced kernel parameters from the allowed list.

tmpfs.description: In-memory filesystems keyed by absolute path.

ulimits.description: Resource limits keyed nofile or memlock.

user.description: User to run as, uid[:gid] or names.

add_prefix.description: Prefix added to the path before forwarding.

certificate.description: Name of an uploaded certificate of the service's server. Needs tls = custom.

cloudflare.description: Cloudflare settings of the hostname. NebulaCtrl always manages the DNS record when the hostname's zone is in the team's connected Cloudflare account. Applied immediately; needs a Cloudflare connection.

component.description: Compose component this domain targets. Required for stacks.

dns_resolver.description: DNS-01 provider code that obtains this domain's certificate.

kind.description: serve the service or redirect to another host.

options.description: Proxy options of the domain. The whole table is one unit: present means it replaces the live option set.

preserve_path.description: Keep the path and query when redirecting.

process.description: Process of a service with processes that this domain routes to. Absent means the service's own process, or the only process with a port. Apps only; stacks use component.

redirect_to.description: Target hostname of a redirect. Required when kind is redirect.

strip_prefix.description: Remove the path prefix before forwarding.

target_port.description: Port of the service this domain targets. Defaults to the service port, or to the port of the process the domain routes to.

tls.description: Certificate mode: auto, custom or none.

www_redirect.description: Also serve www.<host> as a redirect to the host.

server.description: Default server, by name, of this environment. Overrides the root server.

services.description: Overrides of services for this environment. Keys merge over the base service; the source key is optional.

variables.description: Environment-layer shared variables. They override the project layer for this environment only.

content.description: File text. Stored in the service config as plain text: never put secrets here. Exactly one of content and source.

mode.description: File mode as an octal string.

source.description: Path, relative to nebula.toml, of a file whose content is used; the caller supplies it as an attachment.

auto_deploy.description: Deploy on every push to the branch. Needs connection. Applied immediately.

connection.description: Name of a git connection (Team settings → Integrations). Credentials stay in the connection. Needs repo.

repo.description: Repository as owner/name on the connection.

submodules.description: How submodules are checked out: auto, on or off.

url.description: Clone URL (https, http, git, ssh or git@host:org/repo.git). Credentials in the URL are rejected. Exclusive with connection and repo.

watch_paths.description: Monorepo filter: only pushes touching these globs deploy; a leading ! excludes. Replaces the whole list. Needs connection. Applied immediately.

capabilities.description: Driver capabilities, for example compute and utility.

count.description: Number of GPUs, or -1 for all.

command.description: argv of an exec check; the first element is CMD or CMD-SHELL.

deadline_seconds.description: Seconds the deploy waits for the service to become healthy.

path.description: Path probed by an http check. Must start with /.

port.description: Port probed by an http or tcp check. Defaults to the service port.

start_period_seconds.description: Seconds after start during which failures are ignored.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds before one probe counts as failed.

type.description: Probe type: http, tcp, docker, exec or none. Defaults to http when the service has a port, else none.

command.description: The command as an argv array, run without a shell.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds before the command is killed. Needs command in the same table.

command.description: The process command as an argv array, run without a shell in the service's image.

cpus.description: CPU limit of the process in cores. 0 or absent means the service's limit.

health_check.description: How a new container of this process is judged healthy. Same keys as the service's health_check; the default port is the process's own.

memory_mb.description: Memory limit of the process in MiB. 0 or absent means the service's limit; otherwise at least 6.

port.description: TCP port the process listens on for HTTP. 0 or absent means no HTTP port. Ports are unique across the service's processes.

scale.description: Replicas and autoscaling of this process. Applied immediately.

singleton.description: The process never runs two instances at once: the old container stops before the new one starts, and scaling is off.

stop_grace_seconds.description: Seconds a container of this process gets to stop before it is killed. Absent means the service's value.

average.description: Requests allowed per period on average.

period_seconds.description: Length of the period in seconds.

trusted_proxy_depth.description: Number of trusted proxies in front, so the real client IP is limited.

regex.description: Go regular expression matched against the request URL.

allow_cidrs.description: CIDRs allowed to reach a tcp route. UDP routes cannot be restricted.

deny_cidrs.description: CIDRs refused even when allow_cidrs admits them.

health_path.description: Path probed to verify the upstream. Must start with /.

insecure_skip_verify.description: Do not verify the TLS certificate of https upstreams.

listen_port.description: Host port a tcp or udp route listens on.

open_to_internet.description: Publish a tcp or udp route to everyone. Required when allow_cidrs is empty.

pass_host.description: Forward the original Host header to the upstream.

protocol.description: Route protocol: http, tcp or udp. Create-only.

proxy_protocol.description: PROXY protocol version sent to a tcp upstream: 0, 1 or 2.

scheme.description: Upstream scheme of an http route.

server_name.description: TLS server name used to verify https upstreams.

upstreams.description: Upstreams, 1 to 20. Each is { address = "host:port" } or { service = "slug", port = 1234 }. Replaces the list.

verify_skip.description: Skip the post-apply verification of an upstream that legitimately answers with 5xx.

basic_auth.description: Require basic authentication. Enables only: users and passwords are never in the file.

large_uploads.description: Allow request bodies that take minutes to send, for example container registry layer uploads.

request_headers.description: Headers added to requests, name = value.

response_headers.description: Headers added to responses, name = value.

security_headers.description: Security header set: basic or strict (adds HSTS).

keys.description: Variable names that are secret. The file has no value for them.

scope.description: Where the listed secrets are available: runtime, build or both.

git.description: Source key: build the service from a git repository.

stack.description: Source key: a Docker Compose project run as one service.

processes.description: Additional processes that run from the same image, variables, volumes and release as the service, keyed by process name. The service's own port and command are its default process. A process is owned as a whole: a key you leave out takes its default. Processes deploy together; scale is applied immediately.

backups.description: Backup schedules of a database, keyed by a stable key. Applied immediately.

block_egress.description: Block outbound internet access. The service then only reaches its environment's internal network and cannot join shared networks.

build.description: How a git service is built.

command.description: Start command as an argv array, run without a shell. An empty array clears it and uses the image's CMD.

cpus.description: CPU limit in cores. 0 means no limit.

database.description: Source key: a managed database. The keys are create-only.

depends_on.description: Slugs of services that deploy before this one. References in variables add dependencies on their own.

docker.description: Typed container options. Each key is owned individually. Devices, GPUs, runtime and host-level options need an unrestricted server.

domains.description: Domains of the service, keyed by hostname or hostname/path-prefix.

files.description: Config files written into the container before it starts, keyed by absolute path.

generate_domain.description: Attach the platform-generated hostname on the server's base domain when the service has no domain.

git.description: Source key: build the service from a git repository.

health_check.description: How a new container is judged healthy. Each key is owned individually.

image.description: Source key: container image to run, as repo[:tag][@digest]. Registry credentials are never written in the file.

image_retention.description: How many previous images are kept on the server.

memory_mb.description: Memory limit in MiB. 0 means no limit; otherwise at least 6.

name.description: Display name of the service. Defaults to the slug.

networks.description: Names of shared networks to attach the service to. The file never creates networks.

one_shot.description: Run the container to completion on every deploy. Excludes pre_deploy and post_deploy and a port.

only_in.description: Environment slugs in which this service exists in the file. Absent means every environment. Not allowed in environment overrides.

port.description: TCP port the service listens on for HTTP. 0 or absent makes it a worker: no HTTP health check and no domain.

post_deploy.description: Command run after the new release is live. A failure only warns.

pre_deploy.description: Command run before the new release starts. A non-zero exit fails the deploy.

process_name.description: Name of the service's own process (port, command, health_check, stop_grace_seconds, memory_mb, cpus). Only matters when the service has processes: it is the name logs, scaling and domains use for it.

processes.description: Additional processes that run from the same image, variables, volumes and release as the service, keyed by process name. The service's own port and command are its default process. A process is owned as a whole: a key you leave out takes its default. Processes deploy together; scale is applied immediately.

route.description: Source key: an external route to an upstream the platform does not run, or a TCP/UDP exposure.

secrets.description: Names of secret variables of this service. Values are never written in the file.

server.description: Server, by name, the service runs on. Overrides the environment and root server. Required for route services.

singleton.description: The service's own process never runs two instances at once: the old container stops before the new one starts, and scaling is off.

stack.description: Source key: a Docker Compose project run as one service.

stop_grace_seconds.description: Seconds a container gets to stop before it is killed.

tasks.description: Cron tasks that run in the service's image, keyed by task name. Applied immediately.

unset.description: Environment overrides only: TOML key paths removed from the merged service. The removed keys are simply not managed by the file in that environment; nothing live is deleted.

variables.description: Variables of the service, keyed by name. A value is a string using the variable macro grammar, or a table with metadata.

volumes.description: Persistent volumes: name = absolute mount path. Detaching a volume never deletes its data.

compose.description: The compose file as text. Exactly one of compose and compose_file.

compose_file.description: Path of the compose file relative to nebula.toml; the caller supplies its content as an attachment.

resources.description: Per-component limits, keyed by the compose service name. The compose file's own limits win.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds a deploy waits for every component to become healthy.

cpus.description: CPU limit of the component in cores.

memory_mb.description: Memory limit of the component in MiB. 0 means no limit; otherwise at least 6.

command.description: The command as an argv array, run without a shell in the service's image.

concurrency.description: forbid skips a run while the previous one is still running; allow starts it anyway.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds before a run is killed.

timezone.description: IANA time zone of the schedule.

service.description: Slug of a managed service of the same environment and server.

failure_threshold.description: Consecutive failed checks that open an outage.

recovery_threshold.description: Consecutive successful checks that close an outage.

reminder_minutes.description: Minutes between reminders of an ongoing outage. 0 disables reminders.

comment.description: Free-text note shown next to the variable.

public.description: Asserts that a literal value is not a credential, which silences the literal_secret check for this variable. It is not stored.

rotate_every_days.description: Reminder interval, in days, to rotate the value. 0 or absent means no reminder.

scope.description: Where the variable is available: runtime, build or both (build and both need a git service).

value.description: The value, using the variable macro grammar: plain text, references like ${{db.DATABASE_URL}}, generators like ${{secret(32)}}.

description:
NebulaCtrl project file. One file describes a project: services, databases, domains, variables (names and references only), tasks, uptime monitors, backup schedules and per-environment overrides.

Authoring guide:
1. Start from `nebulactrl config export` of the live project, or `config init` for a new repository. Never write the file from memory.
2. Always run validate, then plan, before apply. Read every diagnostic and fix errors by their path, line and suggestions. Apply only a plan with valid: true.
3. Never write secret values. Use `secrets.keys = ["NAME"]`, a generator such as `${{secret(32)}}` or a reference such as `${{db.DATABASE_URL}}`. Never put tokens, passwords or private keys in the file or in URLs.
4. Use only keys from this schema; unknown keys are errors. Keys are snake_case, units are in the key name, variable values are always strings.
5. One source key per service (image, git, database, route or stack); the key decides the kind.
6. Tables merge by key; scalars and arrays replace. Put per-environment values inside [environments.<slug>] and drop keys there with unset.
7. A key you write is owned by the file and overwrites dashboard edits; a key you omit is left alone.
8. Apply stages changes and never deploys; review and deploy them afterwards.

$schema.description: Editor hint pointing at the JSON Schema of this file. Ignored by NebulaCtrl.

environments.description: Per-environment overrides, keyed by environment slug. Environments are never created or deleted by the file.

project.description: Slug of the project this file describes. Checked against the project it is applied to; a mismatch is a blocker.

schema.description: Version of the nebula.toml format. Only 1 exists.

secrets.description: Names of project-layer shared secrets. Values are never written in the file.

server.description: Default server, by name, for every service that does not name its own.

services.description: The services of the project, keyed by service slug.

variables.description: Project-layer shared variables. Services read them as ${{shared.NAME}}. A value is a string using the variable macro grammar, or a table with metadata.
